id_rule: Canonical source IDs are URL-derived hashes. Legacy S### values are aliases only and MUST NOT be joined across datasets because the current atlas and backfill package used colliding S-number namespaces.

sources.title: Joint Statement Announcing the Timeline for the End of the Military Mission of the Global Coalition to Defeat ISIS in Iraq
sources.proof_note: Primary joint U.S.-Iraq statement formally sets a two-phase transition: coalition mission in Iraq ends no later than September 2025 while coalition support against ISIS in Syria from Iraq continues to September 2026 subject to conditions/consultations; practical implementation steps had begun.

sources.title: Some personnel advised to leave US military base in Qatar, diplomats say

sources.title: US-Iran memorandum promised 60 days of calm - it became focus of conflict instead
sources.author: Vanessa Ghanem
sources.proof_note: Regional forward trace: by one month after signature, conflicting Hormuz interpretations had become a major source of renewed confrontation.

sources.title: Iran, US trade air strikes as provisional Hormuz deal awaits approval
sources.proof_note: Reports negotiators reached provisional 60-day ceasefire/shipping terms pending leadership approval while strikes continued.

sources.proof_note: Records a WSJ report about U.S. end-state flexibility; Reuters could not independently verify.
sources.lineage: Reuters report of WSJ; not independent corroboration

sources.title: Oil prices fall on prospect of Middle East ceasefire easing supply disruption
sources.proof_note: Reports Iran reviewing a U.S. 15-point proposal and quantifies large cumulative oil-supply disruption.

sources.title: Trump demands others help secure Strait of Hormuz; allies say no plans to send warships
sources.proof_note: Documents multiple allied governments declining or avoiding naval escort commitments requested by Washington.

sources.title: Last Rounds? Status of Key Munitions at the Iran War Ceasefire
sources.author: Mark F. Cancian; Chris H. Park

sources.title: What’s in the deal between Israel and Lebanon?
sources.proof_note: Explains the U.S.-mediated framework: phased/pilot-zone Lebanese security assumption, verified Hezbollah disarmament linkage, Israeli redeployment, and U.S.-involved coordination/implementation.

sources.title: US aircraft carrier arrives in Middle East, relieving long-deployed USS Lincoln
sources.author: Ben Finley; Konstantin Toropin
sources.proof_note: AP independently reports George Washington arrival to relieve Lincoln; Washington joins George H.W. Bush, showing replacement/continuity rather than disappearance of carrier presence.

sources.title: Saudi Arabia unveils plans for multinational maritime defence coalition
sources.proof_note: Confirms Saudi-led proposed maritime defense coalition; representatives from 43 countries and the EU attended, and 14 countries issued a joint statement supporting the proposed coalition. It does not establish the United States as one of the 14 formal supporters.

sources.title: Iran takes seized ships to port as countries seek information on seafarers
sources.proof_note: Documents Iranian seizure of two container ships after U.S. seizure of an Iranian cargo vessel; includes diversion/turnaround and limited Iranian export data.

sources.title: Statement on the Start of Working Group Meetings of the U.S.-Iraq Higher Military Commission
sources.proof_note: Primary DoD statement that the U.S. and Government of Iraq began the HMC process committed to in August 2023, expressly to enable transition to an enduring bilateral security partnership.

sources.title: War in Iran has cost the US $37.5 billion so far, Pentagon says
sources.proof_note: Reuters reported a Pentagon $37.5B war-cost figure. The reported figure included current and projected costs through Sept. 30, so it is not a clean actual-to-date expenditure total.
sources.lineage: Reuters original reporting of Pentagon estimate

sources.title: Iranian economic collapse may come too late for Trump
sources.proof_note: Finds severe economic strain but continued banking, retail and alternative trade, countering claims of immediate state/economic collapse.

sources.title: US-Iran nuclear talks end in Geneva with progress but no deal
sources.proof_note: Documents the last major pre-war negotiating round, significant progress, no final agreement, and planned technical follow-up.

sources.title: IRGC Navy says Strait of Hormuz closed until further notice
sources.proof_note: Records formal IRGC Navy closure claim following a warning-shot incident.
sources.lineage: Reuters report of Iranian state media

sources.title: Iran says it is reviewing US ceasefire plan
sources.proof_note: Documents a temporary U.S. pause on attacks against Iranian energy plants and Iran’s statement that the proposal was one-sided.

sources.title: Iraq takes full control of air base after US withdrawal, defence ministry says
sources.proof_note: Independent confirmation that Iraq assumed full control of Ain al-Asad after U.S. withdrawal; Reuters ties the departure to the Washington-Baghdad understanding reached in 2024 to transition from coalition presence to a bilateral security relationship.

sources.title: IMF January 2026 WEO Update

sources.title: Full text of the 14-point plan to end the US-Iran war
sources.proof_note: Independent regional publication of the 14-point framework, including blockade removal, toll-free safe passage for 60 days and Oman dialogue on future administration.

sources.proof_note: Records Iran’s threat to lay mines and fully close Gulf access if its coast was attacked.

sources.title: When Satellite Imagery Goes Dark: New Tool Shows Damage in Iran and the Gulf
sources.author: Logan Williams et al.

sources.title: Lebanon has not agreed to shortlist of countries that could verify Hezbollah’s disarmament, official says
sources.proof_note: Corrective/current-status evidence: Lebanese official denied an agreed shortlist and said discussions with the United States were continuing; the State Department confirmed Rome talks addressed third-party verification but did not confirm a final country list.

sources.title: Syrian army says it took control of Shaddadi base after coordination with US, agency says
sources.proof_note: Reports Syrian army control of Shaddadi after coordination with the United States, within the same pre-war U.S.-Syria transition following the Washington-brokered SDF integration arrangement.

sources.title: Gulf economies head for worst crisis since pandemic as war roils energy lifeline
sources.proof_note: Current atlas source for GCC prewar/early-war forecast baseline used in July forecast comparison.
sources.lineage: Reuters source used by current atlas

sources.title: US blockade of Iran will be major military endeavor, experts say
sources.proof_note: Documents start of U.S. blockade against ships entering/leaving Iranian ports after talks failed, distinct from blocking all non-Iranian Hormuz traffic.

sources.title: US, regional partners open new air defense operations cell in Qatar
sources.proof_note: Primary record that a multinational Middle East air-defense coordination cell opened inside Al Udeid’s CAOC immediately before the war.

sources.title: Kuwait Meteorological Center climate station coordinates
sources.proof_note: Official station table gives a Kuwait Airport reference point. Used only as facility-level map geolocation, not as impact coordinates.

sources.title: QatarEnergy-controlled LNG tanker exits Hormuz for first time in nearly three weeks
sources.proof_note: Current atlas source for one LNG tanker transit; not evidence of normalized traffic.

sources.title: One month into Iran war, key US objectives remain unresolved
sources.proof_note: Assesses one-month outcomes and notes continued Iranian missile/drone capability and shifting or unresolved U.S. objectives.

sources.title: Strait of Hormuz transits drop as U.S.-Iran attacks escalate
sources.proof_note: Current atlas source for July Hormuz transit suppression.

sources.title: Two ADNOC tankers attacked by drones in Strait of Hormuz
sources.proof_note: Independent reporting that two ADNOC tankers were hit/damaged; UAE blamed Iran; no casualties reported.

sources.title: Attacks hit major oil and gas sites across Middle East
sources.proof_note: Documents the March 18 South Pars/Asaluyeh strike and subsequent attacks on Gulf energy infrastructure, including major Qatar LNG damage estimates.

sources.proof_note: Documents UNSC condemnation of Barakah attack without attributing responsibility, preserving attribution uncertainty.

sources.title: White House denies US requested ceasefire; new talks may happen in Pakistan
sources.proof_note: Documents competing accounts of who sought the ceasefire and possible second-round talks.

sources.title: China state shippers deploy tankers outside Gulf to avoid chokepoints
sources.proof_note: Documents COSCO/CMES avoidance of Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb and use of ship-to-ship transfer outside the Gulf, evidence of commercial rerouting rather than normalization.

sources.title: Satellite images reveal damage to US bases across Middle East
sources.proof_note: Independent satellite-imagery reporting on damage at U.S. regional bases, including communications-related damage at Al Udeid.

sources.title: Barakah nuclear power plant coordinate record
sources.proof_note: Open-data coordinate reference for the Barakah plant. Used only for facility-level map placement, not BDA or impact geometry.

sources.title: In milestone, US pulls out of strategic Syria base and hands it over to Damascus
sources.proof_note: Independent confirmation that U.S. forces completed al-Tanf withdrawal and Syrian forces took control following coordination between Syrian and U.S. authorities; Reuters also records prior Pentagon consolidation plans and a Washington-brokered SDF integration deal.

sources.title: Iran has no trust in US, will negotiate only if serious, Araghchi says
sources.proof_note: Records Iran’s stated transit regime: most ships could pass if they coordinated with Iranian naval authorities, except designated enemies.

sources.title: Fact Sheet: President Donald J. Trump Solidifies Economic and Defense Partnership with the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia
sources.proof_note: Primary U.S. source documenting the signed U.S.-Saudi Strategic Defense Agreement, regional burden-sharing, and the U.S. statement that Saudi Arabia viewed the United States as its primary strategic partner.

sources.title: Pakistan’s last-ditch effort secures Iran war truce
sources.proof_note: Documents Pakistan-mediated temporary ceasefire and core Iranian demands including Hormuz, nuclear energy and security arrangements.

sources.title: China’s Iranian oil buying curbed by margins, traders say
sources.proof_note: Documents continued Chinese purchases and record March Iranian crude flows to independent refiners, plus large volumes already at sea.

sources.title: Statement from Acting Secretary Cao
sources.author: Hung Cao
sources.proof_note: Official Navy statement: Lincoln will return home as part of a planned rotation; deployment was extended because the mission demanded it; claims 10,000+ sorties and 266 deployed days.

sources.title: Bessent says US will impose toughest ever sanctions on Iran, urges allies and China to cooperate
sources.proof_note: Regional syndication of Reuters Aug. 20 sanctions reporting; useful for reach but not independent corroboration.

sources.title: Hormuz shipping traffic falls to one-week low amid hostilities
sources.proof_note: Current atlas source for eight Kpler-tracked vessels on Aug. 12.
sources.lineage: Reuters source used by current atlas

sources.title: Russia is sharing satellite imagery and drone technology with Iran, WSJ reports
sources.proof_note: Records the WSJ-sourced allegation of Russian support; Reuters said it could not independently verify the report.
sources.lineage: Reuters report of WSJ; not independent corroboration

sources.title: Trump says no talks planned with Iran; Tehran says Hormuz still shut
sources.proof_note: Records directly conflicting U.S. and Iranian claims about talks and whether Hormuz is open; public tracked traffic remained in single digits.

sources.title: Saudi Arabia, Turkey, Pakistan pledge mutual defence as Middle East turmoil escalates
sources.proof_note: Confirms the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement among Saudi Arabia, Türkiye and Pakistan after nearly a year of negotiations; a Turkish official said it was defensive and did not abrogate existing agreements with other states. Reuters identifies all three as U.S. allies.

sources.title: Battered by war, Iran’s rulers wary of more economic pain and unrest
sources.proof_note: Reports July inflation around 66% and food inflation around 128%, documenting severe but not automatically terminal economic strain.

sources.title: Most Strait of Hormuz shipping at standstill despite latest US pledge
sources.proof_note: Documents start of Project Freedom context while commercial shipping remained largely stalled, showing military passage did not equal restored commercial confidence.

sources.title: Some US troops departing Syria, official says
sources.proof_note: Senior U.S. official described the Syria force reduction as a deliberate and conditions-based transition tied to the Syrian government assuming more counter-ISIS responsibility, ten days before the Iran war began.

sources.title: Iran drone and missile attack hits Kuwait airport, state news agency says
sources.proof_note: Documents one fatality and severe terminal damage at Kuwait International Airport while Terminal 4 flight activity provided continuity evidence.

sources.title: Iran war drains U.S. blood and treasure
sources.proof_note: Current atlas source for cumulative U.S. casualty snapshot: 18 service members killed and roughly/more than 430 wounded by July 22.

sources.title: U.S.-Iraq Joint Security Cooperation Dialogue Joint Statement
sources.proof_note: Primary U.S.-Iraq joint statement: both governments committed to a Higher Military Commission to determine how the Coalition military mission would evolve according to ISIS threat, operational/environmental requirements, and Iraqi force capability. It also states U.S. forces were in Iraq at the Iraqi government’s invitation.

sources.title: UAE financial embargo on Iran after missile threat puts rivalry back in spotlight
sources.proof_note: Documents UAE halt to financial/economic dealings after alleging Iranian ballistic missiles targeted maritime traffic; Iran denied the allegation.

sources.title: Iran threatens to go offensive in Strait of Hormuz if diplomacy fails
sources.proof_note: Records expiry of the 60-day negotiating window and Iranian threat of a more offensive maritime posture.

sources.title: Trump warns of economic consequences for any country that supports Iran
sources.proof_note: Records Trump threatening economic consequences for countries providing Iran a lifeline and Treasury promising exceptionally severe sanctions.

sources.title: USAFCENT upgrades CAOC while demonstrating distributed operations
sources.proof_note: Official pre-war evidence that USAFCENT had already operated CAOC functions from Shaw and designed distributed C2 to avoid dependence on one facility.

sources.title: Qatar wants to bolster security partnership with US after Iran strikes
sources.proof_note: Shows Qatar sought stronger U.S. security cooperation after Iranian strikes on facilities including Al Udeid.

sources.title: Pakistan in final truce push as US-Iran deadline looms
sources.proof_note: Regional forward trace of final mediation push before the 60-day window expired and Iran’s stated conditions for reopening Hormuz.

sources.title: Iran Severely Damaged US Air Ops Center in Qatar Soon After War Began
sources.author: Chris Gordon
sources.proof_note: Senior U.S. official/other informed sources: multiple missiles rendered Al Udeid CAOC inoperable; facility was not in use, no injuries; air campaign and later strikes continued from Shaw.

sources.title: AP Iran war escalation and Hormuz shipping report

sources.title: US to deploy thousands of additional troops to Middle East, officials say

sources.title: Trump threatens Iran with power plant strikes over Hormuz blockade
sources.proof_note: Records U.S. threat to strike Iranian power infrastructure and Iran’s threatened response against regional energy, IT and desalination systems.

sources.title: Bessent says US will impose toughest ever sanctions on Iran, urges China to cooperate
sources.proof_note: Records Bessent’s sanctions announcement and focus on China as the dominant buyer of exported Iranian oil; detailed measures were still pending at cutoff.

sources.title: UAE condemns attack on two ADNOC ships in Strait of Hormuz
sources.proof_note: Regional account of ADNOC/UAE statements: two vessels attacked, no injuries, UAE blamed Iran while Iran had not accepted responsibility at publication.

sources.title: Trump threatens to isolate Iran: who are its trading partners?

sources.title: US military begins withdrawing from main base in northeast Syria, Syrian sources say

sources.title: Iran unleashes oil shock to blunt US firepower
sources.proof_note: Reports roughly 97% fall in Hormuz traffic from pre-war levels using UN-related shipping data and explains Iran’s established chokepoint leverage strategy.

sources.outlet: Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS)
sources.title: $3.7 Billion: Estimated Cost of Epic Fury's First 100 Hours
sources.author: Mark F. Cancian; Chris H. Park
sources.proof_note: CSIS estimated first-100-hour costs and reported lower-bound Iranian launch volume of more than 2,000 UAS and more than 500 ballistic missiles.
sources.lineage: CSIS analytical estimate using DOD and partner reporting

sources.title: Two U.S. tanker aircraft leave Bulgaria a month after deployment upset Iran
sources.proof_note: Reuters reports two U.S. tanker aircraft departed Bulgaria on Aug. 21 after a temporary deployment; do not infer Iranian coercive causation from timing alone.

sources.title: Hormuz ship crossings hover in single digits, data shows
sources.proof_note: Kpler/Reuters observation: seven commodity vessels on Thursday Aug. 20, four inbound and three outbound, no VLCC or LNG tanker in that observed set; AIS-dark traffic caveat applies.

sources.title: NATO members discuss Strait of Hormuz options without alliance involvement
sources.proof_note: Interested Allied states coordinated possible national freedom-of-navigation contributions; reporting explicitly says this was not a NATO mission.

sources.title: Iranian oil offers to Chinese buyers fall as U.S. blockade bites, sources say
sources.proof_note: Supports Aug. Iranian crude supply to China near 534,000 bpd versus about 1.4m bpd in 2025, lower floating stocks and buyer substitution behavior; does not establish China abandoned Iran.

sources.title: Iran grants permission for a number of Iraqi oil tankers to pass through Hormuz
sources.proof_note: Supports verified de facto selective passage permission for some Iraqi tankers after repeated Iraqi requests; this does not establish internationally recognized Iranian legal sovereignty over the strait.

sources.title: France and Saudi Arabia discuss alternatives to Hormuz and an energy/logistics task force
sources.proof_note: Supports discussion of Omani loading/port options outside direct Hormuz exposure, pipeline expansion and longer-run logistics alternatives; proposals are not coded as operational infrastructure.

sources.title: U.S., Iran keep up hostile rhetoric ahead of new sanctions
sources.proof_note: Supports Aug. 24 sanctions package being announced/scheduled rather than enacted at cutoff; also records Iranian political/military messages and a later Reuters four-vessel observation for Thursday Aug. 20.

sources.title: Iran says Tehran must overcome unjust sanctions as U.S. ramps up economic pressure
sources.proof_note: Records Qalibaf advocating deeper Iran-Iraq economic links and national-currency trade; this is an Iranian proposal and is not coded as Iraqi acceptance.

sources.title: Iraq aims to boost oil output to 8-10 million bpd in six years
sources.proof_note: Supports Iraqi production target, Saudi/OPEC engagement and export-route diversification via Ceyhan and proposed Baniyas/Aqaba options.

sources.title: New Syria-Iraq crude pipeline still years away, sources say
sources.proof_note: Supports prospective Syria-Iraq/Baniyas route being multi-year and roughly $15B scale; it is not an operating route at the Aug. 22 cutoff.

sources.title: Renewed conflict derails Lebanon’s fragile economic recovery
sources.proof_note: World Bank projects 2026 Lebanon GDP contraction of 6.4% and inflation around 17.5%, attributing renewed deterioration to conflict; record does not assign the entire contraction to Iran or Hezbollah.

sources.title: US tanker aircraft left Bezmer and departed Bulgaria on Friday, defence minister says
sources.proof_note: Bulgarian defence minister says the tanker aircraft departed Aug. 21; deployment was coordinated with Washington and flights were training over allied countries.

sources.title: Defence minister rules out direct national security risk for Bulgaria after reports of possible Iranian threat
sources.proof_note: Bulgarian defence minister said intelligence indicated no direct threat to national security or sites hosting U.S. aircraft; protective measures do not prove attack intent.

sources.title: Parliament authorizes deployment of U.S. aircraft and military personnel at Bezmer Air Base
sources.proof_note: Establishes preexisting temporary authorization window for KC-135 aircraft and personnel at Bezmer, supporting planned-deployment context for the Aug. 21 departure.

sources.title: Iran, Oman discuss resuming talks and Hormuz navigation
sources.author: Arab News / Reuters
sources.proof_note: Reuters-supported regional report citing Oman state news agency: foreign ministers discussed conditions for renewed dialogue and continued Hormuz navigation understandings; no final agreement or Iranian legal control is established.
